newsitem.title: UK: IBCA SAYS ASSIGNS SCOR CLAIMS SETTLING RATING.
newsitem.headline: IBCA SAYS ASSIGNS SCOR CLAIMS SETTLING RATING.

text.p: LONDON, July 15 - IBCA, the European international credit rating agency, has assigned a Claims Settling Ability rating of "AA" (Excellent Security) to the French reinsurance group SCOR.
It is one of the world's largest reinsurers and is listed on the Paris and New York stock exchanges.
SCOR's rating reflects its excellent capitalisation and financial flexibility, diverse revenue base, very strong technical reserves and underwriting expertise.
IBCA has also assigned ratings of "A-1+" to SCOR's short-term commercial paper programme and "AA" to SCOR's long term debt.

The Claims Settling Ability rating applies to the following operating companies in the SCOR group: SCOR, SCOR Deutschland Ruckversicherung AG, SCOR Canada Reinsurance Company, SCOR Italia Riassicurazioni, SCOR UK Group Limited, SCOR UK Company Limited, SCOR US corporation, SCOR Reinsurance Company (US), General Security Insurance Company (US), General Security Indemnity Company (US), SCOR Reinsurance Company Asia Limited, SCOR Asia-Pacific and SCOR Asia-Pacific Australian Branch.

SCOR's principal activity is the underwriting of treaty and facultative reinsurance on a global basis. Total gross premium for 1996 was FRF13.8bln, of which almost 80% was Property/Casualty reinsurance and the balance Life reassurance.
Western Europe and North America are the dominant sources of SCOR's revenues but the group has a growing position in the Far East and emergent position in Central and Eastern Europe.
IBCA believes the group has substantial underwriting skills and its innovative and creative approach to Life product design and development is a significant strength.
Group consolidated assets and net assets at the end of 1996 were FRF38.4bln and FRF6.8bln respectively.
Underwriting performance has been improving and the combined ratio compares favourably with peers.

Technical reserves have been strengthening and are assessed as very strong by IBCA, taking particular note of SCOR's freedom from significant exposure to long-term North American industrial disease and pollution liabilities.
Investment activities have produced a good return on managed assets that has resulted in growing profits and a most satisfactory pre-tax return on equity of 15.6% in 1996.

SCOR is now an established global reinsurance player with unique underwriting specialities in some markets. The group's business is well diversified geographically and by line of business which mitigates the reinsurance portfolio's exposure to adverse localised trading conditions and catastrophes.
IBCA believes SCOR's expertise in Life reassurance provides a strong basis for the development of new and diverse markets.
Although debt gearing is high, capitalisation and financial flexibility are considered excellent and technical reserves very strong.
